en.title: Maximum Profit With Skippable Transactions and Limited Same-Type Streaks
en.description:
The order of the transactions is fixed; each one has a type A..Z and an integer profit, and any of them can be skipped. In the selected sequence, the same type may not appear more than k times in a row. Maximize the profit; selecting nothing is allowed and gives profit 0. A transaction with negative profit may still be worth taking as a separator, so such transactions cannot simply be dropped.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O, editorial and tests; missing original bounds and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the statement.
en.input: The first line contains n k, the second line is the string formed by the n transaction types, and the third line contains n profits; when n=0 the last two lines are empty. The source gives no value bounds and no guarantee that profits are positive; on this site 0≤n≤2000, −10^9≤profit≤10^9, 0≤k≤10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are 18; 199; and 10, checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: dp[c][r] stores the best profit over the processed prefix for a selection that ends with type c repeated r times in a row. For a transaction of type c with profit v, keep the states that skip it; the best profit ending in any other type, or the empty sequence, can be extended to r=1, and type c at r−1 can be extended to r. Update r in descending order so the current item is not reused in the same round.
